title: Measuring the Marginal Value of Sandboxed Emulation for Validator‑Checked LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measured the incremental detection benefit of adding automated sandboxed emulation to a deterministic validator when the same LLM-generated candidate is inspected by both pipelines (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared model "gpt-5-mini" and a deterministic task generator, we evaluated Npairs = 720 confirmatory tasks drawn from three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates. The deterministic validator flagged 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline (validator + sandboxed emulation) flagged 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call accounting reports 721 hosted-model calls (720 shared initial + 1 repair). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report preregistered design, exact quantitative outcomes, an explanation rooted in validator ceiling effects and curated task selection, and prescriptive boundary conditions where sandboxed emulation is likely to matter.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and NetOps workflows. Production assurance requires that generated artifacts satisfy syntactic, ordering, and safety/policy constraints. A widely advocated mitigation architecture layers deterministic validators and (optionally) sandboxed emulation after generation to catch errors that static rules miss. Prior surveys and prototype systems document this practice but provide little large-scale, preregistered evidence quantifying the marginal benefit of adding sandboxed emulation to an already-strong validator. We address this gap with a preregistered, paired confirmatory experiment that isolates downstream guarded-stage effects by reusing the identical sampled candidate for both conditions (shared_initial_candidate semantics).

Research question and contributions. Preregistered research question: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same validator followed by automated sandboxed emulation? Contributions: (1) a machine-readable preregistration and autonomous execution on Npairs = 720; (2) an artifact-grounded paired analysis with exact counts and interval estimates; (3) an artifact-supported interpretation explaining a near-zero marginal effect in this experimental regime; (4) concise operational guidance and reproducibility pointers to the archived execution bundle.
sections.related_work:
Workflow-centred mitigations. Recent surveys and architectural reports document integrating LLM generation with deterministic validators, emulators, and repair loops to raise assurance for NetOps artifacts [1], [2]. Tool-focused studies show that static verifiers capture many structural and policy constraints but can miss runtime-dependent behaviors; researchers therefore often layer emulation to exercise state transitions and temporal interactions that are difficult to exhaustively encode as static rules [2], [3].

Empirical and prototype evidence. Prototype systems and empirical reports show heterogeneous gains from guarded pipelines: in some regimes a verifier alone catches the majority of dangerous errors, while in others emulation reveals subtle runtime failures [2], [3]. These mixed findings motivate a paired design that isolates only downstream contributions (emulation or repair) by holding the generated candidate constant across conditions. Our work provides a preregistered, artifact‑grounded datapoint in that evaluation axis.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and experimental design. We preregistered a paired-binary confirmatory design (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e). The primary estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. The preregistration fixed inclusion/exclusion rules, missingness handling (deterministic reseed up to two times for parser failures), multiplicity procedures, and power planning (minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20). The confirmatory sample targeted Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1,440) and used a deterministic task generator producing intent_configuration_repair_v1 tasks spanning three abstracted vendor-CLI families and three topology templates.

Generation semantics, model, and run accounting. The declared/requested model used in the run was recorded as "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). Shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: exactly one sampled initial candidate was obtained per pair and the identical candidate was presented to both downstream conditions (baseline and guarded) so that any between-condition discordance can only arise in downstream validation, emulation, or permitted repair. Provider-call auditing for the confirmatory execution recorded 721 hosted-model calls in total: stage_counts show 720 calls at the shared_initial_generation stage and 1 call at the repair stage. Condition-level audit fields are reported as counts of provider-call events mapped to logical pipeline stages: the audit shows condition_counts labeled "shared": 720 and "guarded": 1. The apparent asymmetry arises because the shared_initial_generation provider calls produced candidates used by both conditions (one provider call per pair), while the single repair-stage provider call occurred only in the guarded pipeline; thus the provider-call audit reports one set of shared initial calls plus the single guarded repair call.

Baseline validator, guarded pipeline, and repair policy. The baseline validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) implements deterministic rule-based checks: vendor-CLI syntactic parsing, per-command canonicalization, sequence-order checks vs. required_command_sequence, atomicity/workflow constraints (e.g., make-before-break), protected-interface invariants, group-level activity constraints, and final-state conformance. The guarded pipeline runs this validator and then executes the candidate in an automated sandboxed-emulation harness that instantiates the declared topology template and executes normalized CLI commands against vendor-abstracted virtual devices. The emulation maps runtime observations (interface transitions, transient concurrent states, MTU/VLAN application effects, topology-level reachability) to runtime-observation rules that can trigger a guarded detection if they reveal policy or safety violations not encoded in the static validator rule set. The preregistered repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model invocation per task; repair calls are recorded in the execution manifest and provider-call audit.

Inclusion and analysis procedures. Inclusion required vendor-parser acceptance after up to two deterministic reseeds; irrecoverable parser failures would be deterministically replaced per the missingness plan. The primary confirmatory analysis used a paired-binary procedure aligned with McNemar-style exact inference; we report an exact McNemar two-sided p-value and a 95% paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) per the preregistered analysis executor. All numeric results reported below are verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory contingency counts and inferential outcomes (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts are: n11 = 719 (detected by both), n10 = 1 (guarded-only), n01 = 0 (baseline-only), n00 = 0 (neither). Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667). Provider-call accounting: total hosted-model calls = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair), consistent with the audit-stage counts described above. Complete_pair_count = 720 and failed_episode_count = 0 under the preregistered missingness policy.

Discordant-pair attribution. Because of shared_initial_candidate enforcement, the single guarded-only discordance must be attributable to either (a) a guarded-emulation observation not codified as a validator violation or (b) the single recorded repair-stage invocation. The execution bundle archives per-episode traces that link the discordant pair_id to its validator and repair traces; auditors can inspect the archived raw-results and reconciliation artifacts in the canonical execution bundle to locate and examine that unique episode. We do not reproduce raw log excerpts or per-file hashes in this manuscript; the full provenance bundle is archived and cited in the Disclosure Statement for auditor retrieval.

Sensitivity to preregistered design choices. The observed paired difference (≈0.0014) lies far below the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20) used in power planning. There were no irrecoverable parser exclusions in the confirmatory set, so primary analysis used complete paired data without technical-pair exclusions.
sections.discussion:
Why the guarded-stage aggregate benefit was negligible in this regime. The artifact-supported interpretation highlights three principal, nonexclusive causes:

1) Validator ceiling effect and task-rule alignment. The deterministic validator encoded the workflow constraints exercised by the curated task bank (shutdown_configure_restore, make_before_break, paired_link_atomic_mtu_change). The baseline success rate of 719/720 leaves essentially no headroom for emulation to add detections in this constrained distribution.

2) Curated inclusion and reduced adversarial exposure. Confirmatory items were parser-validated and generated deterministically from an intent-aware generator; this reduces the incidence of noisy or adversarial intents that typically expose validator gaps. The absence of parser-exclusion events confirms the bank's tight alignment with validator expectations.

3) Shared_initial_candidate semantics and minimal repair activity. By design we reused the same sampled candidate in both conditions; therefore the guarded pipeline can only add detections via emulation observations or the limited repair policy. Provider-call accounting shows a single repair call across the confirmatory run, corresponding to the unique n10 discordance.

Operational implications. For operator pipelines that maintain a high-coverage static validator tailored to expected intent patterns and that pre-validate inputs, adding automated sandboxed emulation may produce negligible incremental detection at scale. This does not displace sandboxing: rather, it delineates an efficiency boundary. Sandboxed emulation remains important for: (a) noisy natural-language intents, (b) adversarial or fuzzed inputs, (c) greater vendor-CLI diversity, and (d) complex long-running stateful interactions where emulator fidelity exposes runtime side-effects beyond static rules. We recommend a risk-based deployment: invest in validator coverage for routine low-latency automation and deploy guarded emulation selectively for high-risk changes and adversarial testing.

Limitations tied to the archived evidence. The near-zero aggregate effect is specific to the preregistered task bank, the single validator implementation, the declared/requested model, and shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed effect (~0.0014) is therefore empirically precise but far below preregistered sensitivity and must be interpreted as narrowly scoped to this experimental regime. Emulation fidelity and broader vendor/OS diversity remain open variables that could change outcomes in other regimes.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a deterministic validator with the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on a curated synthetic intent→configuration task bank. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Provider-call auditing reports 721 hosted-model calls (720 shared initial + 1 repair). The artifact-grounded evidence attributes the vanishing marginal effect to validator ceiling effects and the curated task design under shared_initial_candidate semantics. These results do not negate guarded pipelines’ value in adversarial, uncurated, or high-fidelity emulation scenarios; they instead quantify a conditional boundary where validator investments can absorb most detectable faults. The archived execution bundle contains per-episode traces and reconciliation artifacts that permit auditors to replicate the reported counts and to inspect the unique discordant episode.

Sandboxed-emulation harness and orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration SHA‑256 recorded in the archive). limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator-ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and a single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across models and validator designs.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and long-lived stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime.
